# Judith Chapter 14 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Judith 14 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/JDT_014_page_001.jpg

---

**1** Judith said to them, "Listen to me now, my brothers. Take this head and hang it on the parapet of your wall.

**2** As soon as morning breaks and the sun rises over the earth, let every man take up his weapons of war, and let every able-bodied man march out of the city. Appoint a commander over them as though you were going down to the plain against the Assyrian advance guard — but do not go down.

**3** They will take up their arms, go to their camp, and wake the officers of the Assyrian army. They will run to the tent of Holofernes and not find him. Fear will come over them and they will flee before you.

**4** Then you and all who live throughout the territory of Israel will pursue them and cut them down in their tracks.

**5** But before you do this, call Achior the Ammonite to me, so that he may see and acknowledge the man who treated the house of Israel with contempt and sent him to us as though to his death."

**6** They called Achior from the house of Uzziah. When he came and saw the head of Holofernes held in the hand of a man in the assembly of the people, he fell on his face and his spirit failed him.

**7** When they helped him up, he threw himself at the feet of Judith and bowed to the ground before her, saying, "Blessed are you in every tent of Judah, and in every nation — all who hear your name will be filled with dread.

**8** Now tell me all that you have done in these days." So Judith told him, in the hearing of all the people, everything she had done. When she finished speaking, the people raised a great shout and filled the city with rejoicing.

**9** When Achior saw everything that the God of Israel had done, he believed in God wholeheartedly and had himself circumcised, and he was incorporated into the house of Israel — and so it has remained to this day.

**10** As soon as morning dawned, they hung the head of Holofernes on the wall. Every man took up his weapons and they went out in companies to the slopes of the mountain.

**11** When the Assyrians saw them, they sent word to their commanders, and they in turn went to the generals, the captains, and all the officers.

**12** They came to Holofernes' tent and said to the one in charge of all his affairs, "Wake up our master — for the slaves have dared to march down against us to give battle, to their own destruction."

**13** Bagoas went in and knocked on the door of the tent, assuming that he was sleeping with Judith.

**14** But when no one answered, he opened it and went into the bedchamber and found him thrown on the threshold, dead, his head taken from him.

**15** He cried out with a loud voice and wept and moaned and shouted and tore his garments.

**16** Then he went into the tent where Judith had been lodging and did not find her; and he rushed out to the troops and cried out,

**17** "The slaves have been treacherous! One Hebrew woman has brought disgrace upon the house of King Nebuchadnezzar! Holofernes is lying on the ground — and his head is gone from him!"

**18** When the officers of the Assyrian army heard these words, they tore their garments, and a terrible distress came over them, and throughout the camp there arose a cry and a very great outcry.

**19** And the men in their tents, when they heard it, were horrified at what had taken place.

---
*LOGOS notes: v. 6 — "his spirit failed him" (exepsychē) preserves the ambiguity of the Greek — the word can mean death but here means fainting. v. 9 — "believed in God wholeheartedly" (episteuse sphodra) — the conversion of Achior is presented with maximum emphasis (sphodra = greatly/wholeheartedly). The circumcision seals his entry into the covenant. v. 13 — "assuming he was sleeping with Judith" — the reader's knowledge against Bagoas' ignorance creates devastating irony. v. 14 — "thrown on the threshold" — not on his bed; the detail emphasizes the indignity of his death.*
